answer: Like a tide that only rises when two shores pull together, each identity is randomly paired with another to finish one joint task per epoch. A real pair must negotiate a shared result, and the work shows it; a sybil farm keeps drawing its own clones as partners, so its pairs produce shallow, self-agreeing output. Each agent guards its own vault of private judgment like onyx, hard, dark, distinct, and only a genuine stranger can test it. Pairings that keep collapsing inward mark one operator wearing many names.
